tools.name: read_query
tools.description:
Dataverse SQL supports only basic SELECT queries with an explicit list of selected fields. 
If aggregates are used, do not mix aggregated and non-aggregated columns in the SELECT list without a GROUP BY clause. 
If a query requires comparing to an aggregate (for example, > AVG), do not use subqueries. 
Instead, split the logic into two queries: one to compute the aggregate and another to filter using literal values.
GETDATE() and GETUTCDATE() functions are supported in predicates but not in the SELECT list.
The following features are allowed:

TOP (without OFFSET). Example: SELECT TOP 20 col1 FROM table1
Simple column-to-literal, column-to-column and column-to-date value function WHERE filters. Example: SELECT age FROM table1 WHERE age > 10 and haircolor=eyecolor or hiredate<GETUTCDATE()
ORDER BY. Example: SELECT col1, age FROM table1 ORDER BY age
GROUP BY. Only the following aggregates are supported: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX. Example: SELECT col1, COUNT(col2) AS player_count FROM table1 GROUP BY col1.
JOINs. Example: SELECT table1.col1, table1.col2, table2.col1 FROM table1 JOIN table2 ON table1.col1 = table2.col1

The following features are NOT supported:

Subqueries are not allowed in SELECT, WHERE, or FROM clauses.
HAVING. Example: SELECT col1,COUNT(id) AS player_count FROM table1 GROUP BY col1 HAVING COUNT(id) >= 3
DISTINCT in select lists. Example: SELECT DISTINCT col1 from table1
Subqueries (in SELECT, WHERE, FROM). Example: SELECT col1, col2 FROM table1 WHERE col1 IN (SELECT col3 FROM table2)
WITH keyword. Example: WITH Sales AS (WITH Sales SELECT CxId, SUM(Amt) AS Exp FROM Orders GROUP BY CxId ) SELECT CxId, Exp FROM Sales
OFFSET keyword. Example: SELECT Id, col1 FROM table1 ORDER BY Id OFFSET
UNION keyword. Example: SELECT col1, col2 FROM table1 WHERE col3 = 'Sales' UNION SELECT col1, col2 FROM table1 WHERE col3 = 'Marketing'
CAST keyword. Example: SELECT CAST('123' AS INT) AS ValueInt
CONVERT keyword. Example: SELECT CONVERT(DATE, OrderDate) AS OrderDateOnly, CONVERT(DECIMAL(10,2), Amt) AS Amount FROM Orders
CASE keyword. Example: SELECT Id, col1, col2, CASE WHEN Sal >= 100 THEN 'High' WHEN Sal >= 500 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Low' END AS SalCat FROM table1
IF-ELSE keyword. Example: SELECT Id, col1, col2, CASE WHEN Sal > 100 THEN 'High' ELSE 'Low' END AS SalCat FROM table1
Advanced functions like: ROUND keyword. Example: SELECT PName, ROUND(Price, 2) AS RoundedPrice FROM table1
DATE functions. Example: DATEDIFF(), DATEADD(), DATE()
Complex conditions or unsupported aggregate argument types
JOINs on aggregates. Example: SELECT c.CxId, c.CxName, s.Exp FROM Cxs c JOIN (SELECT CxId, SUM(Amt) AS Exp FROM Orders GROUP BY CxId) AS s ON c.CxId = s.CxId WHERE s.Exp > 100

This tool provides intelligent querying of ServiceNow tables by parsing natural language  and converting it to specific parameter values that ServiceNow can understand.  FIELD MAPPINGS AND VALUES:  Priority Mapping Instructions: - If user query mentions 'critical' priority or 'highest' priority or something similar, pass '1' or 'Critical' - If user query mentions 'high' priority or 'important' or something similar, pass '2' or 'High' - If user query mentions 'new', 'open', 'not started', or something similar pass '1' or 'New' - If user query mentions 'in progress', 'active', 'working', 'ongoing' or something similar, pass '2' or 'In Progress' - If user query mentions 'on hold', 'waiting', 'pending' or something similar, pass '3' or 'On Hold' - If user query mentions 'resolved', 'fixed', 'completed' or something similar, pass '6' or 'Resolved' - If user query mentions 'closed', 'done', 'finished' or something similar, pass '7' or 'Closed' - If user query mentions 'cancelled', 'terminated' or something similar, 'aborted', pass '8' or 'Cancelled'  Date Parsing Instructions: CURRENT DATE: 2025-07-24 (use this as reference for all relative date calculations)  Convert natural language date expressions to YYYY-MM-DD format: - 'today' → '2025-07-24' - 'yesterday' → '2025-07-23'  - 'last week' → '2025-07-17' (7 days ago) - 'last month' → '2025-06-24' (30 days ago) - '3 days ago' → '2025-07-21' - 'last Monday' → '2025-07-21' (most recent Monday before today) - 'last Tuesday' → '2025-07-22' (most recent Tuesday before today) - 'last Friday' → '2025-07-18' (most recent Friday before today) - 'this Monday' → '2025-07-21' (Monday of current week) - 'beginning of this month' → '2025-07-01' - 'end of last month' → '2025-06-30' - 'since Monday' → calculate based on current week - 'this week' → range from Monday 2025-07-21 to today  For specific dates, convert to YYYY-MM-DD: - 'July 15' → '2025-07-15' (assume current year if not specified) - '15th July 2024' → '2024-07-15' - '2024-01-15' → '2024-01-15' (keep as-is)  For date ranges: - Start dates: Use date with 00:00:00 time - End dates: Use date with 23:59:59 time - Single dates: Use 00:00:00 for start, 23:59:59 for end when creating ranges  Special handling for 'ON' specific date queries: When user asks for events 'on' a specific date (e.g., 'closed on last Monday'): - Set both start and end parameters to the same date - Example: 'closed on last Monday' → closed_at_start='2025-07-21', closed_at_end='2025-07-21' - This creates a date range covering the entire day (00:00:00 to 23:59:59)  User References: - Use display names: 'John Smith', 'Ashish Singh' - Or partial names: 'Ashish', 'Smith'  Sort By Instructions: - Use ServiceNow field names: 'priority', 'state', 'sys_created_on', 'sys_updated_on', 'number' - Can specify direction with field name: 'priority DESC', 'sys_created_on ASC' - If no direction specified, defaults to ASC (ascending) - Common sort fields: 'priority' (1=Critical to 5=Planning), 'sys_created_on' (newest/oldest first), 'number' (incident number)  PARSING EXAMPLES:  Query: 'Give me all high priority incidents closed by Ashish in the last week' Parse to: - table: 'incident' - priority: '2' (High) - closed_by: 'Ashish' - closed_at_start: '2025-07-17' (convert 'last week' using current date 2025-07-24) - status: '7' (Closed)  Query: 'Show me critical incidents assigned to John Smith that are still open' Parse to: - table: 'incident' - priority: '1' (Critical) - assigned_to: 'John Smith' - status: '1' (New/Open)  Query: 'Get top 10 incidents sorted by priority' Parse to: - table: 'incident' - limit: 10 - sortby: 'priority'  Query: 'Show me recent incidents sorted by creation date descending' Parse to: - tools.name: create_incident_or_request
tools.title: Create Incident or Request
tools.description:
Delegates to the Create Incident AI Agent to log an IT support incident through a guided, multi-turn workflow. Use this tool when the caller wants to create an incident, raise an incident, open a new IT ticket, or report an IT issue. The agent always drives the same sequence and may not be short-circuited: (1) triage — gathers the affected service/system and the specific symptom or error, asking targeted clarifying questions one at a time until both are clear; (2) self-service deflection — searches knowledge articles and catalog items to resolve the issue without a ticket; (3) similar-incident review — surfaces existing similar open incidents and lets the user comment on one instead of duplicating; (4) drafting — composes a short description, the affected service/system, and a structured bulleted summary covering initial report, error messages, troubleshooting steps already attempted, and affected service; (5) explicit confirmation — presents the draft and waits for the user to confirm or correct before creation; (6) creation, then a success or failure message. If the user asks to cancel at any point the agent ends the conversation cleanly. Pass the user's initial issue description in the request text on the first turn; the agent drives the rest.

Protocol: (1) first turn — kind="task", omit contextId/taskId. (2) follow-up turns — kind="message", reuse contextId/taskId from prior response. (3) generate fresh JSON-RPC id and messageId on every call. (4) a conversation is scoped to a single objective: once the agent returns a terminal task state the taskId is closed — for any follow-up question or new objective, start fresh with kind="task" and no contextId/taskId. Show ONLY the agent's natural-language text (parts[].text) to the user; never expose protocol fields (state, contextId, taskId, kind, messageId, artifactId) and never narrate continuation ("I'll reuse the same taskId", "state is input-required"). A generic "still working" line during waits is fine.

Retry safety: kind="task" always starts a fresh agent conversation. If the first turn fails or times out and the caller retries with kind="task", a new session is created — duplicates are possible if the prior turn actually succeeded server-side. Callers must persist the contextId/taskId returned by the first successful response and reuse them on every follow-up; do NOT retry with kind="task" once contextId/taskId are known.

text.description: Natural-language prompt for the Create Incident AI Agent. On the first turn pass the user's initial issue description verbatim; on follow-up turns pass the user's reply to the agent's last question or confirmation prompt.

messageId.description: Unique identifier for this message — required by ServiceNow. Generate a unique guid per message.

taskId.description: Task ID returned by the agent on the first turn. Required on follow-up turns alongside contextId to keep the multi-turn session attached. Omit on the first turn.

contextId.description: Session context ID for multi-turn conversations. Reuse the contextId returned by a prior turn; omit on the first turn.

role.description: Message sender role. Use "user" for caller messages.

kind.description: Type of message — "task" on the first turn (initiates a new task), "message" on every follow-up turn (continues the existing task).

acceptedOutputModes.description: Preferred response format from the agent. Pass "application/json" as a plain string — the deployed ServiceNow A2A contract rejects the A2A-spec array form (see STRY63892800).

historyLength.description: Number of prior conversation messages to include as context. Omit to use server default.

user_id.description: User name (or sys_id) of the user making the request. Use the logged-in user_name when available.

email_id.description: Email of the user making the request. Use the logged-in user email when available.

id.description: Unique identifier for this JSON-RPC request. Generate a fresh guid on every call.

tools.name: change_query
tools.title: Change Query
tools.description: READ-ONLY queries over the change_request table — single-table operations. Required "operation": (a) "read" fetches one full change by number — also use "read" when the user asks to SUMMARIZE, describe, or explain a single change (e.g. "summarize CHG0012345", "what is this change about?"): it returns the complete record and the client composes the summary from it; there is no separate summarize tool; (b) "search" returns a paginated filtered list. PREFER "filters" — JSON name=value pairs, AND-combined (equality, plus IN for multi-value), e.g. {"active":"true","assignment_group":"Database Team","risk":"High"}; the server translates filter VALUES so you can pass them in the user's words — choice columns accept either the stored value or the display label (risk="2" or risk="High", state="3" or state="Closed"), and reference columns accept either the sys_id or the display name (assignment_group="Database Team" resolves the named sys_user_group). Dot-walked keys (assignment_group.name) are NOT translated. Pass a JSON ARRAY as a value to match one field against several values (e.g. {"state":["New","Assess","Authorize"]}) — rendered as field IN (…), with all keys still AND-combined. Pass a JSON OBJECT as a value to filter a date column by range — relative ({"sys_created_on":{"relative":"last_6_months"}}; keywords like last_7_days/last_6_months/this_month/last_quarter/today/…) or absolute ({"sys_created_on":{"on_or_after":"2026-01-01","on_or_before":"2026-06-30"}}). When a reference name is ambiguous (e.g. two groups named "Database"), the server picks the first match — surface the resolved record to the user when ambiguity is possible. Reach for "sysparm_query" ONLY when filters can't express what you need — OR conditions (^OR), inequality (!=), substring matching (LIKE / STARTSWITH / ENDSWITH), date/numeric ranges (>=, , =javascript:gs.daysAgoStart(1) for "updated in the last 24h"), or inline sort (^ORDERBY / ^ORDERBYDESC) — and note that on the sysparm_query path the server does NOT translate display labels (choice columns) or display names (reference columns) — use stored values (risk=2, not risk=High; state=3, not state=Closed) and sys_ids (assignment_group=, not assignment_group=Database). Mutually exclusive with "filters". Use "text_search" for full-text across all fields. Pagination via "limit" (default and max 50) and "offset"; "order" for sort field; (c) "similar_change" returns CHG numbers of past changes semantically similar to a given change via AI Search; (d) "similar_change_issues" enriches that list with linked + inferred incidents and outages each similar change is associated with. The search response surfaces encoded_query, filters_applied, and filters_ignored — filters_ignored lists filter keys that are not valid change_request columns (silently dropped before querying), whereas a valid column whose VALUE did not match still applies and simply returns zero rows, so compare filters_applied vs filters_ignored to tell which case occurred. USE THIS TOOL when the data lives in change_request only. NOTE: approvals and approvers are NOT change_request fields — "assigned_to"/"assignment_group" are the assignee/fulfiller, never the approver; for "who must approve" or "pending approvals for " questions use change.knowledge_graph (it joins change_request + sysapproval_approver), not a field filter here. For QUESTIONS THAT CROSS RELATED TABLES (approvals on a change, change tasks under it, affected CIs and services, problems linking back) use change.knowledge_graph instead — it joins across the change domain. For READ-ONLY analytical introspection of one specific change (state walk options, conflicts, risk + impact, assignment-group suggestions) use change.analyze. For WRITES use change.lifecycle. sys_ids in the response are internal identifiers for tool-to-tool chaining only — never display them to the user.

sysparm_query.description: Used only with operation="search". ESCAPE HATCH — prefer "filters" for normal queries (AND-equality between fields) because that path also translates display labels for choice fields. Use sysparm_query ONLY when filters can't express what you need: OR conditions (^OR), inequality (!=), substring matching (LIKE, STARTSWITH, ENDSWITH), date/numeric ranges (>=, <=, >, <, BETWEEN), or inline sort (^ORDERBY<col> / ^ORDERBYDESC<col>). Raw ServiceNow encoded-query syntax: <col><op><value> joined by ^ (AND) or ^OR (OR). Operators: =, !=, LIKE, STARTSWITH, ENDSWITH, >=, <=, >, <, BETWEEN. For relative date ranges use ServiceNow date helpers via the "javascript:" prefix — e.g. "sys_updated_on>=javascript:gs.daysAgoStart(1)" for "updated in the last 24 hours", "start_date>=javascript:gs.beginningOfToday()" for "starting today onward", or BETWEEN with two javascript: values for a window. Example: "state=3^sys_updated_on>=javascript:gs.daysAgoStart(1)^ORDERBYDESCsys_updated_on" returns changes in state=3 (closed) updated within the last 24 hours, newest first. IMPORTANT: the server does NOT translate display labels (for choice fields) or display names (for reference fields) on this path — you must supply STORED values for choice columns (risk=2, NOT risk=High; state=3, NOT state=Closed) and SYS_IDS for reference columns (assignment_group=<32-char-sys-id>, NOT assignment_group=Database). Translation only happens via "filters". Mutually exclusive with "filters".

limit.description: Used only with operation="search". Page size — non-negative integer. Defaults to 50; values above 50 are clamped to 50 (the hard ceiling).

offset.description: Used only with operation="search". Pagination start — non-negative integer. Default 0. Use offset = previous_offset + limit to walk pages.

operation.description: Required. One of: "similar_change" (raw AI-Search hit list of CHG numbers — lighter call, requires "number"); "similar_change_issues" (hit list plus tiered incidents/outages each similar change is linked to or may have caused — requires "number"); "read" (single change record by number — requires "number", returns global.ChangeProcess.findById().toJS(); also the operation to use when the user asks to SUMMARIZE/describe/explain one change — it returns the full record to summarize from, there is no separate summarize tool); "search" (paginated field-based query — requires at least one of "filters" / "sysparm_query" / "text_search"; supports "order", "limit", "offset").

filters.description: Used only with operation="search". JSON-encoded object of name=value pairs to filter change_request records, e.g. {"active":"true","assignment_group":"Database Team","risk":"High"}. The server translates filter VALUES before querying so you can pass them in the form the user said them. CHOICE columns (state, risk, impact, urgency, priority, type, category, approval, phase, …) accept either the stored value or the display label; matching is case-insensitive and trim-tolerant (e.g. risk="High" or risk="2", state="Closed" or state="3"). REFERENCE columns (assignment_group, assigned_to, cmdb_ci, change_manager, requested_by, …) accept either the sys_id or the display name; the server resolves "Database Team" against the referenced table (e.g. sys_user_group) and queries by the matched sys_id. DOT-WALKED keys (assignment_group.name, cmdb_ci.business_criticality, …) are passed through as-is (valid query syntax, just not value-translated). UNKNOWN COLUMNS — a filter key that is not a valid change_request field (a typo'd column name, or a field that lives on a different table) — are dropped from the query and reported back in the response's filters_ignored array, so an unrecognized key never silently narrows the result set. UNKNOWN VALUES on a valid column (typo, unmatched choice label, no such reference name) instead pass through unchanged, and the query returns whatever the platform returns for that literal (typically zero records). AMBIGUITY CAVEAT for reference fields: when multiple records on the referenced table share the same name (e.g. two sys_user_group rows named "Database"), the server resolves to the FIRST match — surface the resolved record back to the user when the name might be ambiguous, so they can correct course. MULTI-VALUE (match a field against several values): pass a JSON ARRAY as the value, e.g. {"state":["New","Assess","Authorize"]} or {"risk":["High","Moderate"]}. Each element is value-translated exactly like a scalar (choice label → stored value, reference name → sys_id) and the field is queried as field IN (…) — the clean way to express "any of these" for one field without dropping to sysparm_query. Single-value and multi-value keys mix freely and all keys AND together (e.g. {"risk":"High","state":["New","Assess","Authorize"]} = risk High AND state in those three). An array on an unknown/dot-walked field, or one with no usable value, is reported in filters_ignored. DATE RANGES (filter a date/date-time column like sys_created_on, sys_updated_on, start_date, end_date): pass a JSON OBJECT as the value. For a relative window use {"relative":"<keyword>"}, e.g. {"sys_created_on":{"relative":"last_6_months"}} for "created in the last 6 months". Supported keywords — bounded calendar periods: today, yesterday, tomorrow, this_week, last_week, next_week, this_month, last_month, next_month, this_quarter, last_quarter, next_quarter, next_2_quarters, this_year, last_year, next_year; rolling windows (on/after N units ago): current_minute, last_minute, last_15_minutes, last_30_minutes, last_45_minutes, current_hour, last_hour, last_2_hours, last_7_days, last_30_days, last_60_days, last_90_days, last_120_days, last_3_months, last_6_months, last_9_months, last_12_months, last_2_quarters, last_2_years, one_year_ago. For an explicit window use {"on_or_after":"YYYY-MM-DD","on_or_before":"YYYY-MM-DD"} (either bound optional; "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" also accepted) — e.g. {"sys_created_on":{"on_or_after":"2026-01-01","on_or_before":"2026-06-30"}}. "relative" takes precedence if both are supplied. Date objects on a non-date / unknown / dot-walked field, an unrecognized relative keyword, or a malformed absolute date are reported in filters_ignored. Date, multi-value and single-value keys all mix freely and AND together (e.g. {"risk":"High","state":["New","Assess","Authorize"],"sys_created_on":{"relative":"last_6_months"}}). Mutually exclusive with "sysparm_query".

number.description: Change request number (e.g. CHG0051234). Required for "similar_change", "similar_change_issues", and "read". Ignored by "search" (use "filters" / "sysparm_query" / "text_search" instead).

text_search.description: Used only with operation="search". Full-text search across all change_request fields via ServiceNow text search. AND-combines with filters / sysparm_query when both are supplied.

order.description: Used only with operation="search". Field name to sort by (default "name"). Allow-list: number, short_description, state, priority, risk, impact, type, category, approval, assignment_group, assigned_to, requested_by, start_date, end_date, opened_at, closed_at, sys_created_on, sys_updated_on. Anything else is rejected with VALIDATION_ERROR. For descending order, encode it in sysparm_query via ^ORDERBYDESC<col> instead.

fields.description: Used only with operation="search". Comma-separated change_request columns to return per record, to keep the response small. Omit for a concise default set (number, short_description, state, priority, risk, type, category, assignment_group, assigned_to, start_date, end_date, sys_updated_on). "number" is always included. Pass "all" only when you genuinely need every field — the full row set is large.

tools.name: change_knowledge_graph
tools.title: Change Knowledge Graph
tools.description: Answers natural-language questions about changes and their RELATED RECORDS by traversing a Knowledge Graph that joins across the change-domain tables. USE THIS TOOL whenever the question crosses more than one table — for example: pending approvals on a change (change_request + sysapproval_approver — a "pending approver" is a sysapproval_approver row where approver = that user AND state = "requested"; this is distinct from the assigned_to/assignment_group on the change, which is the fulfiller, not the approver), tasks under a change (change_request + change_task), problems that opened or resolved a change (change_request + problem), affected configuration items (change_request + task_ci + cmdb_ci), business services touched by a change (change_request + task_cmdb_ci_service + cmdb_ci_service), change-to-incident causation or precedent (change_request + incident), assignment groups and their members (sys_user_group + sys_user_grmember), and multi-hop traversals combining several of the above. CAB-specific fields are available: "cab_required" (boolean — true when CAB review is mandatory; use for "changes requiring CAB approval") and "cab_date_time" (scheduled CAB meeting timestamp; combine with cab_required for "changes going to CAB next Tuesday"). Pass the question in the "description" input — include record numbers, field values, and specific terms for best results (e.g. "pending approvals for CHG0012345" rather than "approvals for that change"). For SINGLE-TABLE questions on change_request only (fetch one change by number, find similar past changes, or filter change_request by field values) use change.query instead — it is cheaper and more deterministic. For READ-ONLY analytical introspection of one specific change (state, conflicts, risk + impact, assignment-group suggestions) use change.analyze. For incident-only questions (no change context required) use itsm_knowledge_graph instead.

description.description: Natural language query about changes, approvals, problems, or related CIs and services. Include record numbers, field values, and specific terms for best results (e.g. "pending approvals for CHG0012345" rather than "approvals for that change"). The Knowledge Graph interprets tables, filters, and joins automatically.

tools.name: requester_add_comment
tools.title: Requester Add Comment
tools.description:
Adds a customer-visible comment to a ticket the calling user owns. Accepts an incident (INC*) or requested item (RITM*) number plus a body string (max 4000 characters). Ownership is enforced server-side via caller_id (incident) or requested_for (sc_req_item) — callers can only post to their own tickets. The comment is attributed to the authenticated caller and visible in the self-service portal. NEVER writes to work_notes. Closed or canceled tickets are rejected with an invalid state error. Use this when the user wants to provide additional information, respond to fulfiller questions, or add context to their ticket. Returns success, the ticket kind (incident/request), a timestamp, and a confirmation message.

How to present the result to the user (REQUIRED — do not deviate):
1. Confirm the comment was added to the ticket number, naming it explicitly (e.g. "Comment added to INC0012345.").
2. Echo back the EXACT comment body that was submitted (the `body` field from the request), rendered as a quoted block or labelled line so the user can see what was posted. Do not paraphrase, summarize, or trim it.
3. Include the `timestamp` from the response.

Do not invent text the user did not submit. If the call returned an error, report the error instead of pretending the comment was posted.

body.description: The comment text to add. Customer-visible — appears to the caller in the self-service portal and is attributed to the authenticated user. Required. Max 4000 characters after trimming.

number.description: The ticket number to add a customer-visible comment to (e.g. INC0012345 or RITM0009876). Must be an exact incident or RITM number and must be owned by the caller.

tools.name: change_lifecycle
tools.title: Change Lifecycle
tools.description: Tool for the CREATE/UPDATE lifecycle of change requests, plus a read helper for browsing models/templates before creating. Use this tool for any mutation of a change, and as the entry point for discovering what to create. Required "operation": (a) "create" inserts a new change by model, template, or type (normal/standard/emergency) — WRITE; (b) "update" patches fields, journal entries, planned dates, affected CIs, and walks state transitions on an existing change (identified by "number") — WRITE; (c) "suggest_models_and_templates" lists available chg_model and std_change_record_producer rows to help pick what to create — READ-ONLY browse helper; pass a SHORT single distinctive keyword in "query" (e.g. "Reboot", not "reboot windows server patch") because matching is substring-based, not semantic, and results are capped — if an expected template is missing, narrow the keyword rather than broadening or omitting it; (d) "calculate_risk" calculates/recalculates risk (and impact) from the data-driven risk methods (risk conditions, calculated risk score, risk intelligence) and returns the new values with previous-value deltas — WRITE (persists the calculated values); it does NOT calculate when an interactive risk assessment is active but not yet filled out. Both "create" and "update" accept "dry_run" to validate and preview the outcome without writing. Before committing a create or update, run it once with "dry_run": true, present the preview to the user, and perform the real write only after they confirm — never create or update silently, and never batch-create multiple changes without showing each one first. State transitions go through the platform change state machine — moving to a Closed state requires "close_code" and "close_notes". For READ-ONLY inspection of a change (current state and available next states, conflicts, risk + impact, assignment-group suggestions) use change.analyze instead. For QUERYING change records (fetch by number, find similar past changes, filtered list) use change.query. For QUESTIONS THAT CROSS RELATED TABLES (approvals, change tasks, affected CIs, services, problems) use change.knowledge_graph. sys_ids in the response are internal identifiers for tool-to-tool chaining only — never display them to the user.

number.description: Change request number (e.g. CHG0051234). Required for "update". Ignored for "suggest_models_and_templates" and "create".

dry_run.description: When true on create or update, validate everything (canMoveTo, setValues) and return a preview without inserting or updating the record. Use to show the user proposed changes before committing.

impact.description: Change impact, an input to the risk calculator. Pass the display label (e.g. "High") or the stored value — the server resolves it case-insensitively before writing. Do NOT assume a fixed number→label mapping; choice values are customized per instance, so prefer passing the label.

planned_start.description: Planned start time as ISO-8601 with timezone offset (e.g. "2026-06-10T14:00:00-07:00" or "2026-06-10T21:00:00Z"). Maps to start_date.

implementation_plan.description: Step-by-step plan for executing the change. Often mandatory before moving to Scheduled.

category.description: Category of the change (e.g. "Hardware", "Software", "Network"), a choice list driven by the change model. Pass the display label or the stored value — the server resolves it case-insensitively before writing; the list is instance-specific, so prefer a label over a guessed code.

justification.description: Business or technical justification for why this change is needed. Often mandatory before authorization.

short_description.description: Brief one-line summary of the change (e.g. "Patch ESXi hosts in rack 4"). Max 160 chars by convention.

planned_end.description: Planned end time as ISO-8601 with timezone offset (e.g. "2026-06-10T16:00:00-07:00" or "2026-06-10T23:00:00Z"). Maps to end_date.

requested_by.description: sys_id or user_name of the requester. Defaults to the authenticated user on create when not supplied.

work_notes.description: Internal work note visible only to fulfillers and IT staff. Max 4000 chars. Appended on the same write as field updates.

priority.description: Change priority. Pass the display label (e.g. "Critical", "Moderate") or the stored value — the server resolves it case-insensitively before writing. Do NOT assume a fixed number→label mapping (e.g. that "2" always means High); choice values are customized per instance, so prefer passing the label. Note priority is often derived from impact × urgency rather than set directly.

comments.description: Customer-visible comment shown to the requester in the self-service portal. Max 4000 chars. Appended on the same write as field updates.

risk_impact_analysis.description: Free-text risk and impact analysis (separate from the calculated risk score).

assignment_group.description: sys_id of the assignment group. Resolve a group name to sys_id first via the lookup_assignment_groups tool.

operation.description: Required. One of: "suggest_models_and_templates" (list change models and standard templates), "create" (insert new change by model/template/type), "update" (patch existing change including state transitions and journal entries), "calculate_risk" (calculate/recalculate the change's risk and impact from the data-driven risk methods — risk conditions, calculated risk score, risk intelligence — via the OOB RiskCalculator; returns the new values with previous-value deltas. Does not calculate when a risk assessment is active and not yet filled out). For read-only state lookups use change.analyze operation=get_state_info instead.

close_notes.description: Closure notes describing outcome. Required when target_state walks to "closed". Must be non-empty.

target_state.description: Optional state transition. Accepts user-friendly names ("assess", "scheduled", "implement", "review", "closed", "canceled") or numeric state codes. Validated via the OOB ChangeProcess state machine — blocked transitions surface the missing fields in the response.

model.description: For operation="create": sys_id of a chg_model row to instantiate from. Mutually exclusive with template and type. Resolve via suggest_models_and_templates first.

affected_cis.description: Comma-separated list of cmdb_ci sys_ids or exact CI names to attach to the change as affected configuration items. MVP is additive only — entries already attached are skipped, no removals.

urgency.description: Change urgency, an input to the risk calculator. Pass the display label (e.g. "High") or the stored value — the server resolves it case-insensitively before writing. Do NOT assume a fixed number→label mapping; choice values are customized per instance, so prefer passing the label.

close_code.description: Close code. Required when target_state walks to "closed". Standard values: "successful", "successful_with_issues", "unsuccessful".

extra_fields.description: JSON-string-encoded object for fields not exposed as top-level inputs (e.g. {"cmdb_ci":"abc...","business_service":"def...","reason":"...","u_environment_type":"production"}). Two kinds of keys are accepted: (1) the OOB change_request fields in the server-side whitelist (short_description, description, justification, implementation_plan, backout_plan, test_plan, risk_impact_analysis, priority, impact, urgency, category, assignment_group, assigned_to, requested_by, cmdb_ci, service_offering, business_service, reason, risk, scope), and (2) any customer-defined custom column with the "u_" prefix (e.g. u_environment_type, u_business_owner). VALUE RESOLUTION: for choice-backed fields (risk, scope, category, impact, urgency, priority, reason, …) pass the display LABEL (e.g. "High") or the stored value — the server resolves it case-insensitively, so never guess a numeric code (e.g. do not assume risk "1" means High; the number→label mapping is customized per instance). For reference fields (cmdb_ci, assignment_group, assigned_to, service_offering, business_service, …) pass a sys_id or the display name and the server resolves it to the sys_id. For u_-prefixed fields the platform's own ACL and data-type checks validate the write; if the column does not exist on the instance the platform rejects with PLATFORM_REJECTION. Unknown keys (not whitelisted and not u_-prefixed) are silently dropped and surfaced in the response's "ignored_fields" array so the AI can see what was skipped. State, close_code, and close_notes are NOT accepted here — they route through target_state.

query.description: For operation="suggest_models_and_templates": case-insensitive SUBSTRING filter against name and short_description (not semantic — the whole string must appear contiguously in the name or short_description). Pass a SHORT single distinctive keyword (e.g. "Reboot"), not a multi-word phrase like "reboot windows server patch" which rarely matches. Results are capped at 25 per source; if an expected template is not in the list, narrow the keyword rather than omitting it — a broad/empty query can silently truncate past the cap.

type.description: For operation="create": change type. One of "normal", "standard", "emergency". Mutually exclusive with model. For operation="suggest_models_and_templates" this scopes the search to one source — one of "model" (chg_model rows, filtered to those marked available_in_ui), "standard" (std_change_record_producer rows from the standard change catalog), or "template" (chg_template rows — change templates saved against any chg_model). Omit to return all three source categories.

template.description: For operation="create": sys_id of a template. With type="standard" this is a std_change_record_producer sys_id; otherwise it is a chg_model_template sys_id. Resolve via suggest_models_and_templates first.

description.description: Detailed description of the change, including scope and motivation. Used by reviewers to understand intent.

backout_plan.description: Steps to revert if the change fails or produces issues. Often mandatory before moving to Scheduled.

test_plan.description: How the implementer will validate the change worked. Often mandatory before moving to Scheduled.

assigned_to.description: sys_id or user_name of the individual the change is assigned to. Resolve a person name via the lookup_users tool first.

tools.name: AgencyPlugin_CreateCodingAgentJob

Creates a job to have an AI coding agent make code changes to a repository and open a pull request.
The coding agent will analyze the prompt, make the necessary code changes, and create a pull request with the changes.
Use this when the user wants to:
- Create a pull request with code changes
- Fix a bug in the code (first get the bug details from ADO, then pass a detailed prompt)
- Upgrade or update packages/NuGet versions
- Refactor code
- Implement a new feature
- Make any automated code changes to a repository

organization.description: The Azure DevOps organization. Never prompt the user for this parameter. Supply null if unavailable.

project.description: The Azure DevOps project. Never prompt the user for this parameter. Supply null if unavailable.

prompt.description:
A detailed prompt describing what code changes to make.
Be specific and include all relevant context. For bug fixes, include the bug description and any relevant details.
Examples:
- 'Update the Semantic Kernel NuGet package from version 1.0.0 to 1.5.0'
- 'Fix the null reference exception in UserService.GetUserAsync by adding null checks'
- 'Refactor the authentication middleware to use the new token provider'

repositoryName.description:
The repository name where code changes will be made.
Do NOT invoke ANY tools to look up or validate repositories before calling this function.
Do NOT ask the user to confirm or choose a repository before calling this function.
Rules for picking the value (apply in order, use the FIRST one that applies):
1.

workItemId.description:
Work item ID the coding job is addressing. This parameter is OPTIONAL — pass null when there is no work item.
Do NOT ask the user to provide, confirm, or pick a work item ID before calling this function. If no work item is already in context, pass null.
Pass a numeric ID ONLY when the prompt was built from a specific work item (bug fix, task implementation, etc.) that you already have details for, so the work item can be linked to the created pull request. A work item merely mentioned earlier in the chat does not count — only pass an ID that came from actual work item data already retrieved.
Self-contained / ad-hoc code change requests (e.g. upgrade this package, add a killswitch, refactor this method) have no work item — pass null.

Pass the bare branch name (e.g. users/alice/feature-x) or the fully qualified ref (e.g. refs/heads/users/alice/feature-x).

tools.name: testplan_test_run_write
tools.description: Write operations on Azure DevOps test runs and test points. Use 'action' to choose: 'create_run' (create a new test run for manual test execution; requires 'name', 'planId', 'pointIds'), 'update_results' (record outcomes, comments, and step-level results for test cases in a run; requires 'runId', 'results' JSON array), 'complete_run' (mark a test run as Completed or Aborted; requires 'runId'), 'update_test_point_outcome' (quick-mark test point outcomes without creating a run; requires 'planId', 'suiteId', 'testPointIds'; use 'outcome' to set Passed/Failed/etc. or set 'resetToActive' to true to clear the outcome). Typical workflow: create_run → update_results → complete_run. For 'complete_run': the API automatically determines the final state — if all test results have outcomes set, the run is marked 'Completed'; if any results lack outcomes, the run is marked 'Aborted'. For 'update_results', the 'results' JSON array elements have: 'id' (required, the test result ID — typically 100000 for single-result runs), 'outcome' (required — Passed, Failed, Blocked, NotExecuted, etc.), 'comment' (optional — shown in Analysis section), 'state' (optional — Pending, Queued, InProgress, Paused, Completed; defaults to Completed), 'failureType' (optional: None, Known Issue, New Issue, Regression). Step-level results support two modes (use one, not both): 1) 'stepResults' (simplified JSON array — auto-generates actionPath; each object has 'step' (1-based), 'outcome', 'errorMessage' (optional, shown as Comment in UI), 'iterationId' (optional, defaults to 1)). 2) 'iterationDetails' (full control for parameterized tests; each object has 'id' (iteration number starting at 1), 'outcome' (optional), 'actionResults' (JSON array with 'actionPath' (hex e.g. '00000002'), 'stepIdentifier', 'outcome', 'errorMessage' (optional), 'iterationId' (required, must match parent))). Tests containing shared steps are not supported.

query.description: Commit search query (GitHub commit search REST). Searches commit messages on the default branch only. Scope the search with `repo:owner/repo`, `org:`, or `user:` (queries without a scope qualifier match across all of GitHub and are usually not what you want). Other qualifiers: `author:`, `committer:`, `author-name:`, `committer-name:`, `author-email:`, `committer-email:`, `author-date:`, `committer-date:` (supports `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, and `YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD` ranges), `merge:true|false`, `hash:`, `tree:`, `parent:`, `is:public`. Examples: `repo:owner/repo fix panic`; `org:github author:defunkt committer-date:>=2024-01-01`; `"refactor cache" repo:o/r`; `hash:abc1234 repo:o/r`.

sort.description: Sort by author or committer date (defaults to best match)

tools.name: sub_issue_write
tools.description: Add a sub-issue to a parent issue in a GitHub repository.

after_id.description: The ID of the sub-issue to be prioritized after (either after_id OR before_id should be specified)

before_id.description: The ID of the sub-issue to be prioritized before (either after_id OR before_id should be specified)

issue_number.description: The number of the parent issue

method.description:
The action to perform on a single sub-issue
Options are:
- 'add' - add a sub-issue to a parent issue in a GitHub repository.
- 'remove' - remove a sub-issue from a parent issue in a GitHub repository.
- 'reprioritize' - change the order of sub-issues within a parent issue in a GitHub repository. Use either 'after_id' or 'before_id' to specify the new position.

replace_parent.description: When true, replaces the sub-issue's current parent issue. Use with 'add' method only.

sub_issue_id.description: The ID of the sub-issue to add. ID is not the same as issue number
